text:
Stephen Halliday is the kind of story an eight-game point streak is built on. A fourth-round pick in 2022 who came up through Belleville, he is now playing 11 minutes a night for Ottawa, up from eight and a half, and on the ice for 45% of the team's power-play chances. He has ten points in 24 games, seven of them on the power play, and scored against the Kings on Saturday. Afterward he told TSN, "I thought in the 2nd period we really got our momentum."

Our numbers call it a breakout, with care. His own chances are up to 1.10 expected goals per 60 from 0.75 (expected goals measure the quality of chances), which is real. At five on five, Ottawa takes 49% of the expected goals with him on, almost seven points worse than without him, and the team has scored about four fewer goals than its chances with him on the ice. Our range has him around 14 goals. The power-play role is the thing to hold onto.
